finding: CNN and Transformer architectures have fundamentally different memory-scaling behavior.
evidence: CNN scaling experiments varied image resolution while Transformer experiments varied sequence length.
why_it_matters: Architecture determines which component contributes most to memory usage.

finding: CNN memory is dominated primarily by activation tensors generated from feature maps.
evidence: CNN activation-memory experiments showed rapid growth as image resolution increased.
why_it_matters: Vision models benefit from activation-aware estimation.

finding: Transformer memory is strongly influenced by sequence length because of self-attention.
evidence: Transformer activation-memory experiments showed increasing memory with longer token sequences.

finding: Transformer parameter memory is substantially larger than the SimpleCNN used in this study.
evidence: SimpleCNN fp32 parameter memory is about 0.36 MB while the Transformer requires about 42.12 MB.
why_it_matters: Large parameter counts make compression techniques especially valuable for Transformers.

finding: Different neural-network architectures require architecture-specific memory estimators.
evidence: The architecture comparison demonstrates that a single estimator cannot accurately model every architecture.
why_it_matters: Future memory estimators should adapt to the architecture being analyzed.
